answer: A network can make each identity pay a slow, verifiable cost before it earns trust: new agents must complete useful work over time, like tending a meadow plot season after season, while a trellis of mutual attestations links each newcomer to established agents who stake their own reputation. A fake identity then faces basalt-hard economics - cloning one agent is cheap, but cloning the whole history of work and vouches costs more than any single attack gains.
